items.stem: According to the foundational scientific text, what artificial industrial process entirely revolutionized global agriculture and effectively provides the complex nitrogen atoms found abundantly in more than half of the human body today?

options.text: The Montreal Protocol

options.label: B
options.text: The Haber-Bosch process

options.label: C
options.text: The Keeling curve

options.label: D
options.text: The Kyoto Protocol

items.answer: The Haber-Bosch process, developed in the early twentieth century, artificially fixes atmospheric nitrogen to efficiently produce ammonia for synthetic fertilisers. This massive industrial breakthrough successfully revolutionized global agriculture by feeding billions of people. Consequently, more than half of the complex nitrogen atoms present in human bodies today originate from this process.

items.stem: Why do urban areas generally experience higher temperatures than surrounding rural areas during hot summer nights?

options.label: A
options.text: Rural areas contain dense forests that actively release massive amounts of carbon dioxide.

options.label: B
options.text: Buildings and asphalt absorb solar radiation during the day and re-radiate it at night.

options.label: C
options.text: Urban centers are completely devoid of any atmospheric greenhouse gases.

options.label: D
options.text: The high albedo of concrete completely reflects all thermal heat upwards.

items.answer: Urban areas are mostly built with materials like concrete, steel, and asphalt, which absorb large amounts of solar radiation during the day. This trapped heat is then re-radiated into the environment during the night, keeping cities significantly warmer than rural areas. This phenomenon is commonly called the urban heat island effect.

items.stem:
Match the specific biological processes of the nitrogen cycle with their correct scientific descriptions:
List–I (Process) | List–II (Description)
P. Nitrogen fixation | 1. Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia
Q. Ammonification | 2. Conversion of ammonia into nitrites and then nitrates
R. Nitrification | 3. Conversion of organic matter into ammonia by decomposers
S. Denitrification | 4. Conversion of nitrates back into nitrogen gas
items.answer: The nitrogen cycle involves several distinct biological processes. Nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric nitrogen directly into ammonia. Ammonification breaks down dead organic matter to produce ammonia. Nitrification then transforms this ammonia into nitrites and nitrates for plant absorption. Finally, denitrification converts the soil nitrates back into atmospheric nitrogen gas, completing the cycle.

items.answer: The geosphere correctly represents the solid parts of the Earth, including landforms like mountains and plateaus. The biosphere encompasses all living organisms and their habitats. However, the cryosphere represents the solid form of water, such as ice and snow, whereas oceans and underground water are components of the hydrosphere.

items.stem: If the direct solar insolation measured on the surface of the Earth is 1 kW m⁻², how much total solar energy is safely received by a 2 m² area in precisely two hours?
items.answer: The total energy received is calculated by multiplying intensity, area, and time. Given an intensity of one kilowatt per square metre, an area of two square metres, and a time of two hours (which equals seven thousand two hundred seconds), the energy equals fourteen point four multiplied by ten to the power of six joules.

options.label: C

options.label: D

items.answer: The diagram illustrates eutrophication, a process triggered when agricultural runoff carries excessive fertiliser nutrients, primarily nitrates, into aquatic ecosystems. This nutrient overload stimulates rapid, unchecked algal growth. As algae die and decompose, the process consumes dissolved oxygen, creating hypoxic conditions that ultimately suffocate and kill fish populations in the ecosystem.

items.answer: The Earth’s atmosphere has a highly structured, layered arrangement based on variations in temperature and composition. Starting from the surface, the lowest layer is the troposphere, followed by the stratosphere which contains the ozone layer. Above these are the mesosphere, the thermosphere, and finally the outermost region known as the exosphere.

items.stem: Read the following statements concerning the active circulation of global planetary winds: 1. Flowing winds are steadily deflected towards the left throughout the Southern Hemisphere. Which of the statements given above are accurate?
items.answer: The Earth’s rotation on its axis prevents planetary winds from traveling in a straight line between pressure belts. Instead, they follow distinctly curved paths. This phenomenon deflects moving air masses towards the right in the Northern Hemisphere and towards the left in the Southern Hemisphere, heavily influencing global atmospheric circulation patterns.
